title.narrative: Indonesia: People Power for Global Justice and International Solidarity

description.narrative: By 2026, an early majority of policy-makers in Indonesia is starting to recognize the importance for fulfilling their obligations to respect, promote, and realize rights for people most affected by a global unjust system (cfr. our domains of change). An early majority of the broad public and civil society acts for systemic alternatives and democratization. They invest in strengthening their structures and policy work.

In Indonesia, 11.11.11 works with organizations and networks that advocate for alternatives for the current unjust system development from a rights perspective. They are committed to fight for democratic-, ecological-, and socio-economic justice. 11.11.11 and partners believe that the current policies, are unable to guarantee economic, social, and cultural rights (ESCR), nor stop the overexploitation of natural resources and the destruction of the environment and biodiversity. Therefore, we have to rethink our current system and develop alternatives, which take into account people’s rights and the planetary boundaries. Our context and actor analyses show that a shift is needed in the way policy-makers are ruling the country and how the private sector acts. We believe that this move has to come from changing the behavior of the broad public and the civil society. 11.11.11 collaborates with national organizations and networks in the field of democratization and human rights, gender justice and ecological justice. These partner organizations are joining forces with rights-holders so that they are better able to defend their rights and undertake joint actions to influence policy. Giving a stronger voice to people in a vulnerable situation is key. The partners also invest in the protection of rights activists and their organizations, as they come under increasing pressure. The partners are part of international platforms through which they promote international exchange and global actions. The collaboration offers partners and 11.11.11 the possibility to strengthen their ties with rights-holders, to develop new or deepen existing collaborations (broader campaigns and coalitions), and to obtain recognition from political actors and the public opinion for the actions they undertake. Key partners are: Walhi, Jatam, Sawit Watch, KontraS and Solidaritas Perempuan

Our target groups are considered lobby and advocacy targets (boundary partners), which are the groups with whom the Indonesia program interacts directly and in whom we anticipate opportunities to influence. These groups are: policy-makers and public institutions, civil society and the broad public. We consider the 11-community as a strategic partner.

description.narrative: R1 Innovators national policy makers and public institutions in Indonesia act and behave to promote systemic alternatives (e.g. in media, parliament), propose changes in legislation and policies (e.g. tax reforms, energy transition) and take measures to tackle their problematic relationship with (trans)national private sector (e.g. on transparency). They invest to improve their relationship with CSOs on our domains of change.

title.narrative: R1 I2 Political innovators are taking concrete initiatives to adapt legislation and procedures

baseline.value: No indication that political innovators are fully playing their role to push for new legislation, to co-operate with other innovators and to work on innovative advocacy.

title.narrative: R1 I1 Political innovators act on the domains of change

baseline.value: No indications that political innovators are fully playing their role of acting and behaving on democratic and ecological justice.

description.narrative: R2 Civil society innovators in Indonesia act and behave in an innovative way (e.g. systemic alternatives) in important structuural injustices that relate to our domains of chagne). They initiate joint actions to change legal frameworks and regulations. They invest in their financial, institutional and political capacities and build strategic alliances to target political and private sector actors.

title.narrative: R2 I1 Civil society innovator in Indonesia act on systemic alternatives

baseline.value: CSO innovators are present but not yet fully playing their role to act and behave on democratic justice, socio-economic justice and ecological justice.

title.narrative: R2 I2 CSO innovators are taking concrete initiatives to adapt legislation and procedures in favor of justice

baseline.value: CSO innovators are present but not yet fully playing their role to push for new legislation, to co-operate with other innovators and to work on innovative advocacy

description.narrative: R3 Broad public innovators in Indonesia are pushing for change on important structural injustices (related to our domains of change). They initiate actions such as social media debates, manifestations, opinions in media, to question the current legal frameworks and regulations and pressure policy makers and private sector to fulfill their obligations.

title.narrative: R3 I2 Broad public innovators are taking concrete initiatives to adapt legislation and procedures

baseline.value: Broad public innovators are present but not yet fully playing their role to act and behave on democratic, socio-economic and ecological justice.

description.narrative: R3 Broad public innovators in Indonesia question the status quo and promote and advocate for alternatives (in media, institutions) in favor of our domains of change. They proactively initiate, support and experiment with exemplary actions on alternatives, and are networking with, and learing from other innovators (policy makers, CSOs, broad public).

title.narrative: R3 I1 Broad public innovators question the status quo and promote and lobby for alternatives

baseline.value: Broad public innovators are present but not yet fully playing their role to act and behave on democratic, socio-economic and ecological justice

description.narrative: R4 By 2026, 11.11.11 invests in a more dynamic Asia 11-community with a large (inter)national network. 11.11.11 facilitates initiatives for the 11-community that strengthen our political impact in/on Asia. 11.11.11 will support the decolonization process and will lead in the development of equal partnerships to eliminate lopsided power relationships.

title.narrative: R4 I2 11.11.11 facilitates and participates in coordinated political strategies on Asia

baseline.value: 11-community is focused on partners of 11.11.11 but can improve coordinated political work and capacity building with members and partners of members. 11-community just started decolonizing.

title.narrative: R4 I1 11.11.11 works in complementarity with the 11-community

baseline.value: High degree of complementarity is reached with member organizations but 11-community can improve capacities and network activities.
